notes:
Overview: Inkwell builds an IDE-integrated copilot aimed at professional developers (IDE plugins for VS Code, JetBrains). Primary ask: sub-100ms perceived TTFT for streaming completions in typical dev workflows and deterministic token-budget behavior to avoid mid-completion truncation.

Key constraints and priorities:
- Low-latency streaming is mission-critical: target TTFT (time-to-first-token) 50-80ms median, p99 < 250ms for local devs on NA regions. Must minimize jitter; jitter spikes cause terrible UX.
- Token budget tuning: want graceful backpressure and soft-fail behaviors. If token budgets are hit mid-stream, we need predictable partial completion (suffix trimming) not abrupt cutouts. Also want per-session token budgeting tied to user plan.
- Model/version pinning: ability to pin a model per release channel (canary/stable) and route fallbacks to lighter quantized variants automatically when latency budgets breached.
- Extension telemetry: VS Code telemetry needs to be correlated with request ids for debugging; they cannot send full source files to Redwood (PII constraint).
- Security/compliance: enterprise customers require SSO (SAML), audit logs for prompt/response, KMS integration, and EU data residency for some accounts.

What we tried so far:
- Internal baseline using open-source model on local GPU: TTFT inconsistent (120-1k ms). Good quality but too much jitter.
- Quick hosted test with competitor A: steady TTFT ~120ms median but token truncation issues under sustained typing and poor prefix caching.

Quotes from calls:
- "If the first token doesn't show up instantly while I'm typing I perceive it as lag — we lose adoption." — Head of Product
- "Need deterministic behavior when budgets run out; customers expect a polite cutoff and suggestion to upgrade, not gibberish." — CTO

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-01-28: Account created; initial intake form.
- 2026-02-02: Intro call (Sofia), covered product overview, asked about TTFT targets. Linked Fireflies: FF_0931_inkwell_kickoff.
- 2026-02-12: Technical deep-dive with SE (Rajan) — walked through current streaming pipeline, VS Code extension constraints, telemetry plan. Action: Rajan to provide POC plan.
- 2026-02-18: Sent POC plan + pricing deck (drive link).
- 2026-02-24: Security questionnaire submitted by Inkwell; legal asked for data residency addendum.
- 2026-03-01: Kickoff POC (2 weeks) — objectives: TTFT profiling across sample workspace, implement prefix caching and token-budget policies, measure perceived jitter and p99 latency.
- 2026-03-05: Mid-POC check-in: initial TTFT median 68ms (NA), p99 310ms with spikes on long prefix loads. Token budget test: under high-concurrency some sessions hit hard limits and stalled. Logged as RDW-5871.

POC goals and success criteria:
- Demonstrate TTFT median < 80ms and p99 < 200-250ms for typical dev machine profiles in NA region.
- Jitter reduction: 90% of requests must have inter-token variance < 15ms.
- Token-budget behavior: when budget exhausted mid-completion, system returns graceful truncated completion plus a standard metadata flag and upgrade CTA. No corrupted tokens.
- Model pinning: show canary->stable routing with automatic fallback to quantized variant when latency SLO breached.

Requirements for Redwood:
- Low-latency streaming with predictable first-byte timing and small jitter.
- Configurable token-budget policies per workspace + clear audit logs.
- Option for private deployment (control plane in customer VPC) for enterprise customers.
- Pricing for dedicated pool (est. peak concurrency 250 realtime connections, sustained 80-100).

Next steps (short):

- Deliver POC report with latency histograms, jitter analysis, and token-budget scenarios by 2026-03-12.
- Legal to review residency addendum; finance to confirm budget by end of March.
